convention.operator: rough one-form Laplacian L alpha_c = -g^{ij} nabla_i nabla_j alpha_c
convention.mixed_product_source: -g^{ij}[(delta_A nabla_i)T_B(j,c)+(delta_B nabla_i)T_A(j,c)] with product terms only
convention.background: all indices raised/lowered and derivatives are background; principal second-symbol and single Gamma_AB terms excluded

terms.label: D1
terms.slot: variation of the derivative-index connection acting on the covariant j-index of T_B(j,c) after i,j contraction
terms.C11_action: zero-order multiplication on the input one-form component alpha_d; integrate <e_r^c, term_c(e_s)>

terms.label: O1
terms.slot: variation of the one-form component connection acting on the output c-index of T_B(j,c)
terms.C11_action: zero-order multiplication on alpha_d; keep free output index c and input index d until basis contraction

terms.label: G1
terms.slot: delta_A acts on the component index d of alpha_d inside T_B
terms.C11_action: zero-order multiplication after relabeling alpha_p as input component

terms.label: G2
terms.expression: + g^{ij} Gamma_B^d_{jc} Gamma_A^p_{id} alpha_p + A<->B is the same contraction as O1 with A,B swapped only after preserving output/input slots; do not double-count as a separate family integral without canonicalization
terms.C11_action: merge with O1 under the final AB symmetrizer if symbolic canonicalization proves equality

canonical_product_operator: P_AB(alpha)_c = -g^{ij}[Gamma_A^p_{ij} Gamma_B^d_{pc} + Gamma_A^p_{ic} Gamma_B^d_{jp} - Gamma_B^d_{jc} Gamma_A^p_{id}] alpha_d + A<->B, with dummy indices canonicalized before integration

not_done: insert explicit h_A,h_B ambient quadratic strain formulas into Gamma_X
canonicalize AB symmetrized dummy indices against basis labels

double_counting_guardrails: Do not add principal second-symbol terms.
Do not add single Gamma_AB derivative terms.
Do not count O1 and G1 as independent after canonical AB symmetrization unless the free output/input slots differ in the contracted basis integral.
Do not claim a C11 number from this table; it is an operator-index cleanup only.
